checks.title: SIEM in place with Microsoft 365, Entra, Intune and Defender sources
remediation: Name the SIEM in the profile's third-party controls.
Route the Entra sign-in and audit logs, the Microsoft 365 audit log, Intune and Defender into it. Microsoft Sentinel counts; so does any other with the connectors in place.
checks.narrative: Without a SIEM the logs live in each portal for their default retention and nobody correlates them. The answer comes from the profile; the Azure collector will later confirm the diagnostic settings behind it.

checks.title: Microsoft 365 backup decision recorded
checks.remediation: Decide and record it in the profile's third-party controls: Microsoft 365 Backup, a third-party product, or accepted risk with the reasoning. Any named answer passes; none does not.

userImpact.text: A decision users never see, until they need a restore.

checks.narrative: Microsoft keeps the service running; it does not restore what a user or an attacker deleted beyond the retention windows. The decision is the control, whichever way it goes.

checks.title: Break-glass accounts tested within the window
remediation: Sign in with each break-glass account.
Confirm the Conditional Access exclusions hold and the alert on its use fires.
Record the date in the profile's operations answers.
checks.narrative: A break-glass account that has not been tested is a password in a safe that may no longer open the door. Twice a year is the common bar.

checks.title: Message Center triage owner named
checks.remediation: Name the person or team that reads the Microsoft 365 Message Center weekly and turns retirements and changes into tickets; record it in the profile's operations answers.

userImpact.text: An admin duty users never see.

checks.narrative: Microsoft retires features and changes defaults on a schedule published in the Message Center. An unread Message Center is how a tenant learns about a change from its users.

checks.title: Secure Score at or above Microsoft's all-tenant average
checks.remediation: Work the not-implemented Secure Score controls by score impact, listed in the scores section with Microsoft's own remediation text. Where this report marks a control covered by a third party, Secure Score will still count it against you.

userImpact.text: Depends on the Secure Score controls worked; each says its own user impact in the Defender portal.

checks.narrative: Secure Score is Microsoft's view and it moves when Microsoft changes the weights. It is reported here beside the posture score, with the differences explained, and never as the grade.

checks.title: Nothing on the expiry calendar within the warning window
checks.remediation: Renew each listed item before its date: rotate the application credential, roll the SAML certificate, renew the Apple push certificate, VPP token or Automated Device Enrollment token, buy or let go the trial or the subscription that is in its grace period, and make sure the federation server has rolled its token-signing certificate and Entra has picked the new one up. The full calendar is in the facts, soonest first.

userImpact.text: No user change if renewed in time; a missed renewal breaks the app or device it covers.

checks.narrative: One calendar for every expiry that takes a service down: application secrets, SAML signing certificates, the Apple push certificate, VPP and Automated Device Enrollment tokens, trial subscriptions, subscriptions in their grace period, and the token-signing certificate of each federated domain, which stops every sign-in in that domain the day it lapses.

checks.title: Entra Connect Health enabled with alerts routed
remediation: Install the Entra Connect Health agent on the sync server and the domain controllers.
Route its alerts to a monitored mailbox or the SIEM.
checks.narrative: Sync stops quietly. Connect Health is the alert that says passwords stopped flowing before the helpdesk queue does. Read through Azure once the Azure collector exists.

checks.title: Microsoft 365 Backup on and protecting every workload
remediation: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, Settings, Microsoft 365 Backup, connect a billing subscription (pay-as-you-go through Azure).
Create protection policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange covering the sites and mailboxes that matter, then all of them as budget allows.
Put a budget alert on the paying subscription (AZ-023) and test a restore.

userImpact.text: Nothing visible; deleted or encrypted content can be restored quickly when needed.

checks.narrative: Retention keeps copies for compliance but restoring at scale after ransomware or a mass deletion is slow and partial. Microsoft 365 Backup restores whole sites, OneDrives and mailboxes to a point in time, quickly. A third-party backup named in the profile covers this check.

checks.title: Secure Score has not fallen in the last 90 days
remediation: Open Secure Score, History, and find the day the score fell.
Look at what changed that day: a control that was turned off, a policy that was removed, a licence that lapsed, or new controls Microsoft added that are not yet met.
Put back what was undone, or record why it was meant.

userImpact.text: Finding what changed asks nothing of users; putting a control back may, as that control says.

checks.narrative: A score that falls means something was undone: a policy removed, a setting switched off, a licence gone. Microsoft keeps 90 days of daily scores, and this compares today with the best day in that time, as a share of the maximum because the maximum moves when Microsoft adds a control. It is a tripwire for drift, not a grade.

checks.title: No subscription is past its term
remediation: For each subscription listed, decide whether it is still wanted.
Renew it in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Billing, Your products, or with the partner it was bought through, before the date shown.
If it is not wanted, move its users to another licence first, so nobody loses a mailbox or a protection the day it is suspended.

userImpact.text: When a subscription is suspended its users lose what it licenses: mailboxes, Office apps, or the security features of the plan.

checks.narrative: A subscription past its term is in a grace period first, then suspended, then deleted with its data. The security features go with it: Conditional Access with Entra ID P1, Defender, Intune. This lists every subscription Microsoft marks as in its grace period, suspended or locked out. Trials that are about to end are on the expiry calendar.

checks.title: No Message Center post is close to its act-by date
remediation: Open each post listed in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Health, Message center, and read what changes on the date.
Do what it asks (a setting to choose, an application to update, people to tell) or decide that the default is wanted.
Record a post that needs nothing from you as an exception, so the next report does not list it again.

userImpact.text: Depends on the change: each post says who is affected and how.

checks.narrative: Most Message Center posts are news. A few carry a date to act by: a setting that flips, a feature that is retired, a default that turns on unless someone chooses otherwise. Missing one is how an organisation finds out about a change from its users. This lists the posts whose date falls inside the warning window, soonest first.
